verses.text: God's promise that we can enter his rest still stands. So let us be careful that none of you fails to enter it.
We have heard the good news, just as they did. But the message they heard did not help them, because they did not join it with faith.
We who believe are the ones who enter that rest. As God said, "So in my anger I made a promise: 'They will never enter my place of rest.'" Yet God's work was finished when he made the world.
Somewhere in the Scriptures he says this about the seventh day: "On the seventh day God rested from all his work."
And in the place we just read he says again, "They will never enter my place of rest."
So some people will still enter that rest. But those who first heard the good news did not enter, because they disobeyed.
So God set another day and called it "today". Much later he spoke about it through David, in the words we already read: "Today, if you hear his voice, do not make your hearts stubborn."
If Joshua had given them that rest, God would not have spoken later about another day.
So there is still a special Sabbath rest waiting for God's people.
Whoever enters God's rest also rests from their own work, just as God rested from his.
So let us work hard to enter that rest, so that no one falls by disobeying, as they did.
God's word is alive and powerful. It is sharper than any sword with two edges. It cuts deep enough to divide soul and spirit, joints and bone marrow. It judges the thoughts and plans of our hearts.
Nothing in all creation is hidden from God. Everything is uncovered and open before his eyes, and we must all explain ourselves to him.
We have a great High Priest who has gone up into heaven: Jesus, the Son of God. So let us hold on firmly to the faith we say we believe.
Our High Priest understands how weak we are. He was tempted in every way, just as we are, yet he never sinned.
So let us come boldly to God's throne, where his kindness is found. There we will receive mercy, and find his kindness to help us when we need it.
